summary: STATUS requires_review -- ONE open blocker awaiting operator adjudication; see blockers[0]. All other work is complete, committed, and green. Set 109 Session 4 of 4, "Correct the registry, put the cheap model where it pays, walk it" -- the set-terminal session. HEADLINE: `python -m ai_router.model_inventory --check` now EXITS 0 for the first time -- all 15 configured model_ids are offered by their provider -- and the check is now WIRED into ai_router/scripts/drift_guard.py, so a commit reintroducing a bad id turns CI red. REGISTRY CORRECTED THROUGH THE CONFIRMATION FLOW, NOT BY HAND: the bare `gpt-5.6` alias (an id OpenAI does not list, silently served from gpt-5.6-sol at twice the recorded rate) is RETIRED and split into explicit gpt-5-6-sol / -luna / -terra entries; `opus` re-pointed to claude-opus-5 (same price as 4.8 -- a free upgrade) and `sonnet` to claude-sonnet-5 ($2.00/$10.00 vs 4.6's $3.00/$15.00, with the 2026-08-31 lapse recorded as a dated pricing: row so the calendar boundary needs no future edit); Fable 5 ADDED (absent from the registry entirely); `gpt-5-5` corrected 2x ($2.50/$15.00 -> $5.00/$30.00, a real id whose rates were copied from gpt-5.4 and never confirmed, so the drift gate passed it); `gemini-3-1-pro` corrected off its self-declared placeholder; `gemini-pro` gained its previously unrepresentable >200k tier; the identity-only `gemini-3-pro` id corrected to gemini-3-pro-preview. EVERY RATE WAS WRITTEN BY `pricing_proposal --apply` FROM THE PROVIDERS' PUBLISHED PAGES -- none hand-typed: 12 accepted, 2 REJECTED (the identity-only claude-opus-5 / claude-sonnet-5 entries, whose rates now live on `opus` / `sonnet`; a second priced surface for one model is this set's origin defect wearing a different hat), each accepted entry stamped confirmed_on 2026-08-04. `gemini-pro`'s pin to 2.5 Pro was RE-CHECKED and deliberately LEFT, with the reasoning in the entry (3.1 Pro costs MORE, its only id is a preview, and the registry calibrates a new model as a generator before trusting it to verify) -- a proposal, not a switch, as the spec directs. COST RECONCILED, LEDGER NOT REWRITTEN: recomputed row by row from each row's own token counts, the ledger reports $177.4150 against a true $228.5689 across 1,237 rows -- understated $51.1539 (28.8%), of which gpt-5-6 is 99.8% at a factor of exactly 2.000. The spec's own figure was ~85x too small (it cited one session's slice). gemini-pro's missing tier cost NOTHING -- not one of its 366 rows exceeded 200k input tokens -- so it is deliberately excluded from the disclosure rather than caveating 366 correct rows. Disclosed in cost_report.py (text + JSON) and s4-cost-reconciliation.md; the raw rows stand. SESSION 3's WAIVED RESIDUAL FIXED: `--fetch` could propose replacing a hand-encoded long-context tier with the page's flat short-context rate, silently deleting the expensive tier. Such entries now go to not_comparable_entries -- reported side by side, never proposed, unreachable by --apply -- on a condition written on the DATA, not the provider name. NEW FAIL-CLOSED GUARD (the set's one BREAKING change for consumer repos): a routable entry declaring no rates now fails config load, because an absent rate reads as $0.00 and the selection paths RANK by that scalar, so it would win every cheapest-candidate tiebreak while billing an unknown amount. UAT WALKED: the confirmation flow run live against the three pricing pages, accepting and rejecting, which found and fixed two readability defects in the diff (a date-tiered rate mislabelled as a size tier; the S3 residual above). 4-item checklist authored from that walk on a throwaway config copy, every command executed first. VERIFICATION FOUND FOUR BLOCKING MAJORS, ALL ACCEPTED, NONE DISPUTED -- see s4-remediation-round-1.md. Two were correctness defects in code this session wrote (an exit code that certified unchecked rates as clean -- a sibling-site miss of L-069-1 four lines from a fix I had just made; and a cost disclosure that applied the correction factor to post-fix rows, i.e. the same defect it discloses, reversed). One was a deferral whose stated reason had expired AND was factually wrong. THE FOURTH CAUGHT THIS SESSION VIOLATING ITS OWN SPEC'S RISK REGISTER: the discovery fan-out was pinned to gpt-5-6-luna on price alone, where the spec says the pin "should move only with evidence, not with the price list". THE PIN IS WITHDRAWN -- route(prefer_model=...) and verification.discovery.model ship complete and tested, the config line is committed COMMENTED OUT above a note naming the experiment that would arm it. What evidence exists points the other way: on the same diff, Luna's 2 discovery calls returned 1 Major while Sol's single supplementary call returned 3 more, two of them the correctness bugs above. prefer_model is deliberately a route() ARGUMENT rather than a new task_type, because route() gates the dynamic orchestrator exclusion on task_type == 'session-verification' and a new type would have silently dropped the only guarantee that a session is not verified by its own provider -- a conclusion an independently routed design review (Anthropic excluded) reached unprompted.
blockers: ROUND 4 (gpt-5-6-sol, remediation-review) -- Major, ACCEPTED AS REAL, NOT REMEDIABLE BY THIS SESSION, awaiting operator adjudication. It accepted all four prior fixes and then found that withdrawing the Luna discovery pin leaves an explicit end-of-set deliverable unmet: spec.md's Session 4 step 3 and 'Ends with' require 'the discovery fan-out runs on the cheap variant'. Round 2 had raised the opposite Major -- that arming the pin violated the same spec's risk register ('the pin should move only with evidence, not with the price list'). With no evidence in hand the two clauses cannot both be satisfied, and producing the evidence properly (both variants over several past bundles with known findings, against a threshold declared in advance) is a work item, not a remediation step. Per the constitution's escalation ladder this was NOT re-rounded; a third-provider opinion was taken instead (operator pre-authorized): routed with anthropic AND openai excluded -> google/gemini-2.5-pro, which answered that the risk control must prevail over the deliverable, that forcing an n=1 comparison would be 'precisely the kind of corner-cutting Clause B is designed to prevent', that the session delivered the MECHANISM and its ACTIVATION was out of scope -- and that 'the decision to close a session that cannot meet a deliverable due to a conflicting internal control belongs to the operator'. THE OPERATOR'S DECISION, one of: (1) close as-is, recording lunaOnFanOut as deliberately unmet pending evidence (the third provider's recommendation, and the orchestrator's); (2) commission the Luna-vs-Sol evaluation as a follow-on and arm the pin only if it clears a predeclared threshold; or (3) direct the pin armed on the existing reasoning. Arming it is one uncommented line in router-config.yaml under verification.discovery; the mechanism ships complete and tested either way. Full record: s4-remediation-round-1.md and s4-third-provider-adjudication.json.
